public_rationale: Under the stated model-building reading, a prepublication counterexample exists. Araujo and colleagues used cognitive theories of discourse comprehension to change BERT-style architecture and pretraining. That directly contradicts a blanket claim of ignoring the literature and does not rely on researchers merely probing an existing model. The finding is scope-sensitive: it does not establish that dominant GPT-style systems incorporated these theories.
limitations: The result includes BERT-style pretrained language-model methods within the claimed approach.
One substantive counterexample does not establish widespread engagement with the literature.
The paper does not implement Kintsch's particular comprehension model.

our_interpretation: Read the firm statement as alleging a lack of substantive use of the described literature in building language models.
Examine architecture, training objectives, and model-building methods. Research that only probes an existing model or mentions the literature does not qualify.
The relevant literature includes cognitive accounts of how discourse representations arise; the claim is not restricted to implementing Kintsch's particular model.
Include pretrained BERT-style language-model methods, while flagging that restricting 'the approach' to dominant GPT-style systems would change the assessment.
Assess model-building methods documented by 2022-06-22, including earlier methods still relevant then. No arbitrary annual window is imposed.
criteria.support_condition: Representative design documentation and a sufficiently comprehensive contemporary review establish that the model-building approach did not substantively use the specified meaning and comprehension literature.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented prepublication language-model architecture or training method explicitly uses that literature to change how discourse or meaning representations are learned.
